differences.explanation: tshark exposes the payloads of two non-final IPv4 fragments as data. pcaplens records IPv4 and buffers them until the datagram completes; it has no opaque data layer.
tshark's frame.protocols adds data for the five-byte synthetic HTTP response body. pcaplens retains its length and SHA-256 under HTTP metadata rather than creating a body-protocol hierarchy node.

reference_normalization.counts: packets containing a layer, not repeated record occurrences
